subject: Post-demo: Talonworks integration & routing policy - next steps
messages:
From: Elena Malkov <elena@talonworks.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@talonworks.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Talonworks integration & routing policy - next steps

Hi Aditya / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo today — helpful walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a list of asks so we can scope an integration plan: 

- Goals: (1) low-latency chat (interactive support) for US-based customers, (2) cost-efficient nightly batch embeddings & reranking for search index updates, (3) structured tool-calling for our ticketing system (strict JSON responses).
- SDK / Auth: we currently prefer mTLS for backend-backend calls but are open to API-key based server-side auth if it maps to our VPC setup. Need your recommended auth pattern for your Private deployment and hosted API fallback behavior.
- Routing / policies: want primary routing to a low-latency hosted region (us-west), auto-failover to dedicated capacity in us-east or eu-west for capacity/regional outage. Also want simple cost thresholds so non-interactive requests route to cheaper quantized variants.
- Reranker / embeddings: plan to run nightly embeddings and then a two-stage rerank (ANN top-100 via vector similarity, then cross-encoder rerank top-10). Need guidance on latency/cost tradeoffs and any recommended model pairing.
- Instrumentation: sample tracing/logging hooks (token-level billing breakdowns), and example SLOs we can monitor from the Console.

Attaching our high-level MVP requirements. Can you put together a short mutual-action plan (owners, timeline, blockers) and a proposed routing-policy snippet we can review? Also please propose times for a 45m technical follow-up next week with your solutions engineer and one of our backend leads.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Malkov
Head of Platform Engineering, Talonworks
---
Attachment: talonworks-MVP-reqs.pdf (summary deck, 4 pages)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Malkov <elena@talonworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv@talonworks.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 18:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Talonworks integration & routing policy - next steps

Elena — great notes, thanks for pulling these together. High level answers + next steps below.

Short answers:
- Auth: for Private we recommend mTLS for inter-service comms and a short-lived API key token for app calls. Hosted API supports strong API keys + optional IP allowlists; we can also set up an mTLS gateway for Dedicated if you want the same posture across environments.
- Routing: primary low-latency path = hosted us-west cluster (gpu-optimized runtime). Fallback chain we suggest: hosted us-west -> dedicated us-east (reserved) -> hosted eu-west (regional fallback). Cost policies: tag requests by intent (interactive/batch) and map interactive->low-latency model variants, batch->quantized cheaper variants.
- Reranking: two-stage approach matches our guidance. Cross-encoder rerank is more expensive; we can provide a cost delta estimate once you share average doc lengths and queries per second.
- Structured output/tool-calling: we recommend function-calling with strict JSON schemas for your ticketing workflows; we’ll provide an example schema and a guardrail to validate outputs before actions are executed.

Attached is a first-pass routing policy draft (redwood-routing-draft.yaml) and an initial mutual action plan below.

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- Week 0: Technical follow-up (45m) — introduce Karthik (solutions) + Monica (CS) to Talonworks infra lead — owner: Aditya — target: 8/23 10:00am PT.
- Week 1: Sandbox SDK & auth PoC — Aditya/Karthik provide SDK quickstart + example config — owner: Karthik — deliverable: working low-latency chat route in sandbox.
- Week 2: Reranking PoC & perf numbers — Monica leads on data ingestion + test runs — deliverable: cost/latency report for the two-stage reranker.
- Week 3: Rollout plan & SLA doc — finalize routing policies, fallbacks, and monitoring.

Links & attachments:
- SDK quickstart: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/quickstart
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765
- Attachment: redwood-routing-draft.yaml

Questions before the call: can you share a representative sample of documents we’ll index (size distribution) and an expected QPS for the chat feature? That will let us size the reranker and provide a cost delta for cross-encoder.

Thanks — look forward to the follow-up.

—
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0147

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Talonworks integration & routing policy - next steps

Elena / team — adding some technical notes that we can flesh out on the call: 

1) SDK & auth
- Sandbox path: server SDK (node/python) with API key + JWT delegation to user sessions. For production Private, mTLS between services + short-lived tokens for app servers. We can provide an ingress example (Envoy mTLS + token exchange).

2) Structured output / tool-calling
- Recommend function-calling (RPC-like) with a strict JSON schema per ticket action. Validate output server-side with the schema; if validation fails, route the request to a conservative fallback model variant.

3) Embeddings + reranker
- Recommended pipeline: nightly batch -> vector store (FAISS/Annoy/managed) -> ANN recall top-100 -> cross-encoder rerank top-10. For cost savings, use a lightweight embed model for recall and a smaller cross-encoder tuned for your domain.
- Expected perf: ANN recall (ms per query depending on index) + cross-encoder (50-200ms per candidate on GPU). We'll quantify once you share sample sizes.

4) Routing policy (example snippet)
- primary_route:
  - region: us-west
  - variant: low-latency (non-quantized)
- fallback_chain:
  - - dedicated-us-east: reserved-pool
  - - hosted-eu-west: regional-fallback
- intent_routing:
  - interactive: primary_route
  - batch: quantized-variant (cost-optimized)
  - tool_call: strict-schema -> if schema-fail -> safe-mode-variant

5) Observability hooks
- Token-level cost breakdown, per-request latency histogram, model-version tags, trace IDs forwarded to your tracing system. We can include an example Kibana/Console dashboard.

I'll prepare a short YAML policy example and a sandbox quickstart for the call.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is great.

Confirming the 8/23 10:00am PT slot for the technical deep-dive. We'll prepare a 2000-document sample (sizes ~100-2,000 tokens) and send it before the call so you can run a quick perf pass.

Two quick Qs for prep:
- Can you ballpark the incremental cost of adding the cross-encoder rerank step vs using only ANN+dot-product? Our rough guess is ~2-4x per-query but would value a Redwood estimate.
- For tool-calling, would Redwood recommend optimistic execution (execute after schema passes) or a staging step (place actions in a queue for manual review)? We're leaning conservative for first 6 weeks.

We'll upload the dataset to the Drive link and share access. Thanks for the fast turnaround on the YAML and MAP.

Best,
Elena
